record.tranche_reason: The post reports prompt-based tests of whether sampled features activate on human-generated subcomponents, but does not compare SAE dictionary sizes, feature directions, or whether child features partition a parent feature's inputs.
record.gate_note: The post cites prior meta-SAE work, but reports no results from it. Its own measurements concern responses to generated subcomponent prompts, not feature splitting across dictionary sizes.
record.test_reason: The post tests whether single pretrained Gemma Scope features fire on ChatGPT-generated subcomponent phrases. It compares no dictionary sizes, does no parent/child latent analysis, compares no directions and tests no other objective. Its results bear on no version of the claim. It cites meta-SAE work only as motivation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that SAE features are often less decomposable than their descriptions imply. Many features can be decomposed intuitively but many cannot, which may indicate opaque model behaviour. The prompting method has acknowledged limitations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ChatGPT-generated subcomponents and phrases, then measures activation of individual pretrained Gemma Scope features; it does not train or compare SAEs of different sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: The post notes that generated descriptions can fail to capture the character patterns that activate features, and that better prompting might change outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: About 35% of sampled layer-20 Gemma Scope 16k features fired on all five ChatGPT-generated subcomponents. Some were narrower than their labels, and about a third could not be activated by the prompting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How well human-intuitive semantic subcomponents predict an SAE feature's activations varies widely across features, and prompt-based probing misses features tied to surface patterns.

record.problems: The author says the generated prompts may fail to capture true feature behavior, a larger number of features should be analyzed, and feature decomposition is noisy and difficult to define rigorously. The number of sampled features is not stated.

untested.parts: All: no comparison of dictionary sizes, replacement, input coverage or direction.
All: no comparison across scales or SAE families.
All: no nested families and no geometry.
All: no test of parent latents failing to fire where child latents take over, and no variation of size or sparsity.
All: no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents, and no test for novel latents.
All: no test of the training objective and no Matryoshka comparison.

record.verdict_notes: A low-evidence LessWrong post (score 1). It gives no sample size, controls or uncertainty. The record's relation and tranche of discusses/T6 are appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: No SAE size comparison, replacement of a smaller feature, input partition test, or direction comparison.
No scaling comparison or test across SAE families or large models.
No measurement of nested feature families or their geometric proximity.
No parent-child latent takeover test, or comparison across SAE sizes or sparsity levels.
No comparison between larger- and smaller-SAE latents, or test for novel latents.
No test of whether the SAE objective produces splitting, or comparison with another objective.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The post was inspired by the meta-SAE work and looks at whether features decompose, using prompts. It tests no claim version.

tranche.reason: The post tests whether single features fire on prompt-generated subcomponents. It compares no dictionary sizes and does not use the finding as a tool.

source_check.notes: The post does not state how many features were sampled. The 16k residual width comes from the Neuronpedia URLs, not the prose. The post attributes many failures to prompt artifacts. The prose names feature 6772 but the link goes to feature 6722.

statements.correction: Layer 20, Gemma 2 2B, Gemma Scope residual 16k SAE (width from Neuronpedia URLs). About 35% produced activations across all five generated subcomponents; some features activated on narrower subsets than their Neuronpedia descriptions; around a third gave no nonzero activations, largely from prompt artifacts.
